description: We’re fascinated by space and love imagining the future. I’m the Space Bear, full of imagination, always coming up with out-of-the-box ideas and exploring new ways to apply them. The Space Dog studied physics, and her knowledge-based, rational thinking gives my imagination wings.
summary:
Space Cadet is a cooperative browser game for one to four players. Players design an outpost or spacecraft, choose scientific instruments, and operate their mission over ten turns. Each player proposes a response to changing events, and the commander reviews the crew’s decisions before executing a shared plan.

The game makes engineering trade-offs visible before each decision. For example, pointing a solar-powered spacecraft toward the Sun can improve power generation, while pointing it toward Earth can improve data transmission. Only mission-relevant data that reaches Earth earns science credit.

Players can compare the effects of changing one setting, consult NASA and ESA learning references, and download a mission report to review their decisions. Space Cadet helps learners understand how design choices, limited resources, and teamwork shape what a mission can accomplish.
details:
Space Cadet lets one to four players design and operate a space mission in a browser. The commander selects a mission, a vehicle or outpost, and scientific equipment. Players can invite teammates or fill empty seats with autoplay. Over ten turns, the crew works toward science, observation, and safety or lifetime targets while responding to changing conditions.

The initial design determines which operating choices are available and what they cost. Outpost crews manage oxygen, water, food, recycling, and shelter. Spacecraft crews balance observation, cooling, pointing, communications, and fuel. Each player submits a proposed response. The commander reviews the proposals and checks whether the shared plan is feasible before executing the turn.

The game’s creative feature is the ability to compare the consequences of a single change before committing to a decision. For example, players can compare Sun-pointing and Earth-pointing settings while keeping other choices fixed. This makes it easier to see why a decision that improves power generation or data transmission may reduce observation time. The mission score reinforces the same lesson because scientific observations earn credit only when relevant data reaches Earth.

Our goal is to help learners practice engineering judgment and teamwork. Turn forecasts show the expected effects of a plan, and a downloadable PDF records the crew’s decisions, trade-offs, and possible experiments for a replay. NASA and ESA references in the guide and learning materials explain principles behind spacecraft systems, mission design, and operations. The simulation uses simplified values and timescales suited to an educational game.

We built the browser interface with React and TypeScript, used Vite for development and builds, and used Node.js for the multiplayer room API and server-side saves. We used Playwright and Microsoft Edge for browser checks. The game includes interactive SVG illustrations, browser-synthesized music, and English and Korean interfaces.
